tickers.cause_summary: Shares closed +10.98% at $30.82 in a sharp rebound ahead of its Q2 report, fully recovering the late-July selloff triggered by the FTC/Utah/LA County lawsuit over subscription and data-sharing practices (the close was ~5% above the pre-lawsuit July 28 level). The move was amplified by the broad risk-on rally and by pre-earnings positioning around the second-half EBITDA margin ramp.

First Solar was the best S&P 500 performer, up as much as 14% intraday, on positioning ahead of the U.S. Commerce Department's Section 232 polysilicon tariff decision expected in early August, a catalyst Wall Street (e.g. Wells Fargo's $320 target) had been flagging for weeks. The market-wide relief rally and falling yields added fuel.

No company-specific news; Coherent (close ~$288 vs $262.89 prior) rose with a sector-wide risk-on move in AI optical networking names (Lumentum, AAOI) driven by strong hyperscaler capex/AI data-center optimism and the broad Nasdaq +2% rally, with earnings not due until Aug 12.

SolarEdge rallied with the whole solar complex on the pending Section 232 polysilicon tariff decision and lower rates/oil, plus positioning one day ahead of its Aug 5 Q2 earnings report; no SolarEdge-specific announcement was found.

Oracle jumped 9.22% to $141.85 as the tape rallied on Trump calling off strikes on Iran, with additional support from its newly expanded Google Cloud partnership, a five-year defense contract worth $3.3B (up to ~$7B), and renewed confidence in converting its ~$638B backlog into AI cloud revenue.

Builders FirstSource, a high-beta housing/rate proxy, bounced with homebuilding and building-products names as Treasury yields retreated from 18-month highs and oil fell ~6% on the Iran de-escalation, following its late-July Q2 report; no fresh company-specific catalyst was found for Aug 3.

Vertiv rose ~8.9% on continued follow-through from its strong Q2 (revenue +24%, margin expansion) and bullish AI/liquid-cooling data-center demand commentary, amplified by the broad tech/AI risk-on rally and analyst targets near $336.

WisdomTree extended gains after its July 31 record Q2 results (record $162.9B AUM, adjusted EPS $0.31, 780bp margin expansion), with Oppenheimer raising its price target to $22 from $21 on Aug 3 and asset-manager/risk-asset sentiment strong in the market-wide rally.

DigitalOcean surged in sympathy with the AI-cloud complex (CoreWeave +11%, Nebius +8%) during the risk-on rally, and on positioning the day before its Aug 4 Q2 report following its pre-announcement of record results with RPO above $800M.

Ares climbed ~8% as a wave of post-earnings price-target hikes landed after Friday's in-line Q2 (RBC to $168, Oppenheimer to $151, Deutsche Bank to $144, TD Cowen to $155), citing strong fundraising and fee-related earnings, with lower yields and the broad rally easing private-credit fears.

Palantir reported Q2 2026 results after the Aug 3 close that CEO Alex Karp called "otherworldly": revenue up ~93% year over year to ~$1.94B, U.S. commercial revenue up ~149%, adjusted EPS $0.41, and full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to about $8.15B. Shares posted their best day in more than two years on Aug 4.

Gartner reported Q2 CY2026 results on Aug 4 that beat Wall Street on both revenue (~$1.68B, roughly flat y/y) and profit, sparking a ~23% squeeze in a heavily beaten-down stock trading far below its 52-week high.

Entegris beat Q2 estimates (adjusted EPS $0.93 vs ~$0.82 expected; sales $883.2M vs ~$835M consensus, with adjusted gross margin 47.6%) and guided above consensus, and the move was amplified by a broad semiconductor rally (SOXX +6%) that day.

Westlake released Q2 2026 results pre-market on Aug 4 showing a sharp profitability rebound on higher product pricing (EPS ~$2.01 on ~$3.27B revenue), and investors rewarded the earnings beat and improved operating performance.

Whirlpool reported Q2 on Aug 3 (revenue missed, down 6.8% y/y) but held its investor call the morning of Aug 4, where CEO Marc Bitzer's team reaffirmed the 2026 outlook (~1.5% like-for-like growth, ~4% ongoing EBIT margin, ~$300M free cash flow) and pointed to sequential margin gains and North America strength, triggering a relief rally in a deeply depressed stock.

Marvell previewed next-generation AI memory and storage products (including the Bravera SC6 PCIe 6.0 SSD controller) as the FMS 2026 memory/storage conference opened, and drew aggressive AI-related price target hikes; the move was magnified by the day's broad AI/semiconductor rally.

A Reuters report that the Trump administration/FCC is drafting a ban on imports of new Chinese optical transceiver modules and data center hardware sent U.S. optical component names sharply higher (AAOI +16%, Lumentum +11%, Corning +8%), with Coherent seen as a prime beneficiary; several banks also raised targets (e.g., JPMorgan to $435).

Adeia reported Q2 2026 on Aug 3 (revenue ~$96M, slight miss; adjusted EPS $0.34 vs $0.31 consensus, 59% adjusted EBITDA margin, plus disclosure of a multi-year Google/YouTube TV license renewal); after an initial after-hours drop the stock reversed sharply higher on Aug 4. No separate Aug 4 headline catalyst was found, so the move looks like an earnings-driven reversal.

No Intel-specific news on the day; the stock rode a powerful sector-wide semiconductor rebound (PHLX Semiconductor Index +6%, SOXL +20%) as the AI trade recovered from July's tariff-driven washout, helped by policy headlines favoring domestic chip/hardware suppliers and continued enthusiasm over Intel's blowout Q2 reported in late July.

Super Micro rose with the broad AI server/semiconductor rally on Aug 4 and on positioning ahead of its own fiscal Q4 results due after that day's close; no company-specific news drove the intraday gain.

Freshpet reported Q2 2026 results after the Aug 4 close that beat on the top and bottom line (net sales +15.5% to $305.6M, adj. EBITDA $52.2M, adj. EPS ~$0.39) and raised its full-year 2026 sales and adjusted EBITDA guidance. The Aug 5 move was amplified by a squeeze, with roughly 21% of the float held short.

Shake Shack reported Q2 2026 results on Aug 5, with EPS of $0.43 versus ~$0.32 expected and revenue up 17.2% to $417.6M (slightly below revenue estimates), same-Shack sales +3.5%, easing labor costs, and affirmed FY2026 sales guidance of $1.6-$1.7B.

Dynatrace reported Q1 fiscal 2027 results on Aug 5 with adjusted EPS of $0.48 vs $0.44 consensus and revenue of $554.5M (+16% y/y) vs $549.3M expected, plus an upbeat profit outlook (Q2 revenue $565-570M) and $275M of buybacks in the quarter.

IFF reported Q2 2026 results (released after the Aug 4 close, call Aug 5) showing ~6% sales growth across all segments, raised full-year EBITDA guidance, and announced a $2.5B buyback plus a use-of-proceeds plan for the Food Ingredients divestiture; headline revenue/EPS looked light largely because of the divested business being moved out of continuing operations.

Continued follow-through from Supernus' Aug 3 announcement of an all-stock merger of equals with Indivior (1.5401 Indivior shares per SUPN share) alongside Q2 2026 revenue of $219.1M (+32%, a beat) and raised FY2026 guidance; no separate Aug 5-specific catalyst was found.

SharkNinja reported Q2 2026 before the open on Aug 5 with net sales up 22.2% y/y to $1.77B and EPS of $1.26 versus roughly $1.08-$1.14 expected, driven by strong domestic and international growth; the sales surge lifted shares sharply.

Coeur rose with a broad precious-metals rally on Aug 5 as gold jumped roughly 4% toward ~$4,247/oz and silver climbed above $62/oz on much weaker US labor data, softer real yields and a weaker dollar; Coeur's own Q2 2026 results were only released after the Aug 5 close, so the intraday move was metals-driven.

Hecla closed +7.5% at $16.54 on Aug 5 as silver and gold surged, with its Q2 2026 report the same day showing record/near-record free cash flow ($136M consolidated), record Lucky Friday silver output, $483M cash and no long-term debt.

Newmont rallied with the Aug 5 gold spike (bullion up ~4% on weak US jobs data and firming Fed rate-cut expectations), helped by bargain-hunting/valuation reset after its post-Q2-earnings pullback from the July 23 report.

Kratos reported Q2 CY2026 after the Aug 4 close with revenue up 30.5% y/y to $458.8M (a beat), adjusted EPS of $0.21, record backlog and raised/optimistic full-year organic growth guidance (Q3 revenue guided to $460-480M), sending shares up on Aug 5.
First Advantage reported Q2 2026 results on August 6, 2026, with revenue of about $448.8 million and net income of $16.9 million, and raised its full-year revenue guidance.

MACOM reported fiscal Q3 2026 results before the open on August 6, 2026, with revenue up 35.8% year-over-year to $342.2 million, gross margin expanding to 58.3% and operating income more than doubling, driven by AI/data-center optical demand.

No company-specific news found for Semtech on August 6, 2026; the move appears to be sympathy/sector strength in AI data-center connectivity chips following MACOM's blowout fiscal Q3 report and guidance that morning (Semtech is a frequent high-beta mover on semiconductor sector news).

ATI Inc. reported Q2 2026 results on August 6, 2026, exceeding the high end of its guidance (sales $1.26B, EPS $1.09, adjusted EBITDA margin up 440bps to 22.6%, record $4.4B backlog) and raised its full-year outlook.
DNOW reported Q2 CY2026 results on August 6, 2026, with revenue up 108% year-over-year to $1.31 billion (3.1% beat) and adjusted EPS of $0.12 versus $0.09 expected, sending the stock sharply higher.

Remitly reported Q2 2026 results after the close on August 5, 2026, beating estimates on revenue, customer growth and margins and guiding Q3 revenue to $505-507 million (20-21% growth); shares jumped ~9% after hours and carried the gain into August 6.

e.l.f. Beauty reported fiscal Q1 2027 results after the close on August 5, 2026 (revenue +36% to $479.4M, EPS $1.75 vs ~$0.69 expected, Rhode contributing ~$160M) and raised FY2027 guidance; after an initially negative after-hours reaction the stock reversed and closed up ~6.9% on August 6 as investors and analysts warmed to the beat-and-raise.

Versant Media reported Q2 2026 results that beat estimates and raised its full-year outlook, while declaring a $0.375 quarterly dividend and announcing an additional $100 million buyback after completing a $100M accelerated repurchase.

Leidos reported strong Q2 2026 results on August 4, 2026 (revenue $4.56B, +7%; non-GAAP EPS $3.26; $5B in bookings) and again raised full-year guidance; the August 6 gain appears to be continued post-earnings follow-through amplified by a wave of analyst price-target hikes (e.g., RBC to $230, Truist higher).

US Foods reported Q2 fiscal 2026 results and hosted its earnings call on the morning of August 6, 2026, posting accelerating volume growth, record adjusted EBITDA and margin, ~10% adjusted EBITDA growth and 21% adjusted EPS growth.

Doximity reported fiscal Q1 2027 results after the close on Aug 6, 2026 with revenue of ~$156.6M beating consensus (~$151.7M) and raised its full-year sales outlook; shares went vertical on Aug 7 after CEO Jeff Tangney said on the call that the company's AI search product is profitable and driving adoption.

Twilio posted a Q2 2026 beat (revenue ~$1.50B, +22% y/y; adjusted operating income ~$284.6M) with bullish forward guidance, credited to broad messaging/voice volume strength and AI-driven demand; the stock gapped from just under $195 to close at $241.28 on Aug 7.

Halozyme reported record royalty-driven Q2 2026 results (non-GAAP EPS $2.28 vs ~$1.82 consensus, revenue +48%) and sharply raised full-year 2026 guidance (EPS to $8.65-$9.00, revenue to $1.835B-$1.910B), which also drew analyst upgrades on Aug 7.

Five9 reported Q2 2026 revenue of $312.4M (vs ~$307M est., +10% y/y) and adjusted EPS of $0.70 above estimates, with subscription revenue accelerating for a third straight quarter and full-year AI growth guidance raised to at least 60%.

Tandem Diabetes' Q2 2026 report showed sales of ~$254.6M, a much narrower net loss, notable gross-margin improvement from the PayGo model shift, and reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance with Mobi momentum highlighted, sparking a large relief rally on Aug 7.

Airbnb beat on Q2 2026 results (EPS $1.37 vs $1.25 est.; revenue $3.61B vs $3.58B est., +17% y/y) and issued a stronger-than-expected outlook showing booking demand held up beyond the World Cup boost, driving a breakout above prior resistance.

Fluor delivered a large Q2 2026 earnings beat with a surging backlog after a weak first quarter, alongside portfolio-reshaping news (selling an equity stake) and new international awards including Bahrain infrastructure/FEED work.

Celsius rebounded after Rockstar Energy founder Russ Savage disclosed a ~4.7% stake (over 12 million shares, ~$300M) and publicly demanded the removal of CEO John Fieldly, offering to take the CEO job himself, one day after a weak Q2 report.

Microchip reported fiscal Q1 2027 sales of ~$1,484.7M with non-GAAP EPS of $0.76 above its own $0.67-$0.71 guidance and gross margin of 63.8%, then guided Q2 revenue up to ~$1.589B, signaling an analog/MCU cycle recovery.

Coherent extended a multi-day sector rally (up ~41% on the week) on the Reuters-reported Aug 4 draft FCC/administration measure to bar imports of new Chinese optical transceiver models, a policy that would hand Western optics suppliers a large share of a ~$26B market; its own earnings were not due until Aug 12.

MarineMax announced a definitive agreement to be acquired by Safe Harbor Marinas, a Blackstone affiliate, for $53.00 per share in cash, alongside a strong fiscal Q3 report showing a swing back to profitability and gross margin up 530bps to 35.7%. Reports also framed it as a potential bidding-war situation, and the stock closed near the deal price with a ~1.75% spread.

Helmerich & Payne hit a new 52-week high after Barclays raised its price target to $50 from $47 (Overweight) and other firms (Evercore ISI, Susquehanna) reiterated buy ratings following its Aug. 6 fiscal Q3 beat and raised outlook; the move was amplified by a ~3% surge in crude on the Strait of Hormuz closure that lifted the energy sector ~3%.

Datadog extended its post-earnings rally as a broad wave of Wall Street price-target hikes (Citi, Morgan Stanley, Baird, BMO, Raymond James, Canaccord, Needham, Cantor, Oppenheimer) into the $280–$327 range landed after its Aug. 6 Q2 beat (revenue $1.12B, +36% y/y) and raised FY26 guidance, with analysts highlighting 750+ AI-native customers and an OpenAI renewal.

SM Energy rallied with the entire oil and gas complex as WTI jumped ~3.5% to about $81 and Brent topped $86 after Iran added conditions to reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi forces struck a Saudi refinery; the S&P energy index gained roughly 3%, with high-beta E&Ps moving several times that.

APA Corporation surged along with other upstream E&P names on the crude spike tied to the continuing Strait of Hormuz closure and dwindling hopes of a near-term Iran deal; no company-specific catalyst was reported for the day.

Everpure (the former Pure Storage, now trading under ticker P) jumped after Susquehanna upgraded the stock to Positive from Neutral and lifted its price target to $120 from $85, citing its AI data-platform positioning; momentum traders piled in through the session.

Northern Oil & Gas rose with the oil-driven energy rally (Hormuz closure lifting crude ~3%) while investors continued to digest its Q2 beat, with revenue up 16.6% y/y to $745.2M and reaffirmed shareholder-return plans.
Talos Energy, a high-beta offshore Gulf E&P, moved with the sector as crude prices surged on the Iran/Strait of Hormuz standoff; no Talos-specific news was found for Aug. 10, 2026.

BioMarin hit a 52-week high as analysts including Canaccord Genuity raised price targets following the company's Aug. 6 Q2 update, which showed ~20% revenue growth, raised FY26 revenue guidance to $3.875–3.925B, strong Voxzogo sales, and accretion from the Amicus Therapeutics acquisition.

PBF Energy, a pure-play refiner, rallied with the energy complex as crude and product cracks jumped on the prolonged Strait of Hormuz closure and a Houthi strike on Saudi Arabia's Jizan refinery, which tightened global refining supply.

Datadog surged ~11.5% on heavy volume in a sharp snapback from the roughly 19% post-earnings selloff of Aug 6, as sell-side analysts (including Oppenheimer) hiked price targets and highlighted AI-native demand — over 750 AI-native customers, all ten of the largest AI companies, and OpenAI renewing as its largest customer — following a Q2 beat with ~36% revenue growth.

Super Micro reported fiscal Q4 2026 results after the Aug 11 close with profits well above estimates, a sharp non-GAAP gross margin rebound, and blowout guidance (FQ1 revenue $14.5-15.5B vs ~$12B consensus and FY2027 revenue of $65-72B vs ~$52.5B consensus). Shares led S&P 500 gainers on Aug 12 and analysts raised targets, though some (e.g. Goldman) questioned margin durability.

H&R Block reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter and full-year results after the Aug 11 close, beating on EPS ($2.38 vs $2.21 expected) with revenue and cash-flow growth, an increased dividend and large buybacks, plus a confident fiscal 2027 outlook.

CAVA reported Q2 CY2026 results after the Aug 11 close, with revenue up 31% to $368.4M beating estimates and comparable sales up ~9% on strong traffic; the stock jumped ~14-16% on Aug 12 despite a 60bp decline in restaurant-level margin.

Viavi had already reported its own results on Aug 5; the Aug 12 jump was sector sympathy after Lumentum's blowout fiscal Q4 report and optical/AI datacenter demand outlook lifted the entire optical networking and test group.

Ciena rallied ~11-13% on read-through from Lumentum's blowout quarterly results and strong AI-optics demand commentary released after the Aug 11 close, with the broader technology-equipment/optical group up sharply and some sell-side target hikes.

No company-specific catalyst found for Aug 12; DigitalOcean rose with a broad rally in cloud/software-infrastructure and AI compute names driven by strong CoreWeave and Super Micro results and continued positive analyst sentiment after its Aug 4 Q2 report.

Dell rose ~10% on read-through from Super Micro's much-stronger-than-expected AI server outlook (and strong CoreWeave results), reinforcing the AI-infrastructure demand narrative ahead of Dell's own September report.

Coherent jumped ~8-9% as rival Lumentum's strong earnings and outlook boosted optical networking sentiment, with investors also positioning ahead of Coherent's own fiscal Q4 report scheduled for after the Aug 12 close (amid ongoing talk of US restrictions on Chinese optical transceivers).

HPE climbed ~8% to a record close on the same AI-server demand read-through from Super Micro's guidance beat and CoreWeave's results, amid a broad technology-equipment sector rally and bullish analyst price targets.

MaxLinear rose ~8% in sympathy with the optical/AI-datacenter complex after Lumentum's blowout results, extending strength in its optical interconnect and infrastructure product narrative; no MaxLinear-specific news on the date was found.

Reuters reported Workday was in advanced takeover discussions with private equity firm Silver Lake, talks reportedly ongoing for months; the stock spiked roughly 18-20% (hitting ~$220 intraday with a volatility halt), adding about $8.6 billion of market value.

No BlackLine-specific news found for the date; the move appears to be sympathy buying in beaten-down mid-cap SaaS names after the Workday/Silver Lake leveraged-buyout report reframed them as private equity targets, amplified by the soft PPI print and rate-cut optimism that lifted the whole software complex.

Reporting on the day described DocuSign jumping ~8-10% to roughly $63-64 on broad sector strength rather than company news, i.e. the software-wide rally driven by cooler wholesale/consumer inflation data and the Workday buyout-speculation read-through to cheap, cash-generative SaaS names.

No GDDY-specific catalyst on the day beyond routine items (a small CAO stock sale filed that day and a recent Wedbush AI-themed coverage initiation); the gain looks like participation in the broad internet/software rally on the soft PPI report and record S&P 500 close.

Intraday coverage on Aug 13, 2026 flagged UiPath trending up ~5% and extending a bullish trend with no fresh company-specific news; the move fits the agentic-AI/enterprise-software rally on cool inflation data rather than a UiPath event.

No dated Aug 13 company release found (Q2 earnings were Aug 6); the payments name rallied with high-beta fintech/growth stocks on the softer PPI and rate-cut expectations, with supportive analyst commentary in the background.

No CoStar-specific announcement located for the day; it rallied with the broad tech/real-estate-data complex on the cooler inflation prints and lower yields, following the CEO's early-August open-market purchase of 83,300 shares that had already improved sentiment.

No new Five9 catalyst found on Aug 13 (its big earnings-driven jump was Aug 7); the move appears to be continued momentum plus SaaS-wide strength on soft inflation data and takeover speculation across small/mid-cap cloud software after the Workday-Silver Lake report.

No StepStone-specific news found for that date; as a private-markets asset manager it benefited from the cool PPI/rate-cut trade and from the Workday LBO headline signaling a revival of large private equity deal activity.

RingCentral rose ~7.8% to about $67.78 with no company announcement identified; the move tracks the depressed-valuation SaaS group that rallied on the Workday buyout report and the softer inflation data.

No ticker-specific catalyst found for August 14, 2026; MaxLinear had already risen ~3% the prior session and the move appears to be part of a broad semiconductor rally that week following softer-than-expected US inflation data and continued AI-chip enthusiasm.
No clear catalyst found for Copart's August 14, 2026 jump; no earnings release, M&A, or analyst action was located for that date, so the driver is unidentified.

Cognex closed up ~6.6% at about $65.63 on August 14, 2026 (per market-data commentary), but no company-specific news was found; the move looks tied to the day's strength in semiconductors/factory-automation names and the stock's strong ongoing momentum (YTD +~83%).

AMD closed up 6.5% at about $514.13 after pricing a $4.75 billion bond offering to fund AI/data-center expansion, on top of continued enthusiasm from its Advancing AI event where management raised its AI chip TAM projection to roughly $1.4 trillion by 2030.

No dated company-specific news was found for Peabody on August 14, 2026; the gain appears to reflect the ongoing coal/AI-power-demand thematic bid (including US policy support for coal-fired generation) rather than a discrete event.

Solaris Energy Infrastructure rose ~5.7% to about $63.30 on August 14, 2026 with no company announcement identified for that day; the move looks like continued momentum in data-center/behind-the-meter power infrastructure names.

MP Materials rose ~5.5% to about $58.74 on August 14, 2026 with no specific dated announcement found; commentary that period attributed strength to continued US government support for domestic rare earths and firm rare-earth pricing.
Fox reported fiscal Q4 2026 results on August 6, 2026, so the August 14 move was not the earnings print itself; no clear catalyst for that specific date was found.

Reporting around that period described NRG gaining as investors revisited its data-center power pipeline and its reaffirmed 2026 guidance (adjusted EBITDA of $5.325-$5.825B, EPS $7.90-$9.90) from the Q2 release; no separate August 14 announcement was found.

Vishay surged along with other semiconductor/analog and memory names (grouped with Western Digital and FormFactor in same-period coverage of chip stocks skyrocketing), following cooler inflation data and sector-wide AI/analog demand optimism; no Vishay-specific news that day was located.

No single fresh catalyst found for the session; MaxLinear extended a multi-day run (up ~3-5% on Aug 13) as investors kept bidding its pivot to AI/optical data-center infrastructure after Q2 revenue grew ~55% year over year and after early-August AI partnership announcements (Everspin, Core Micro Systems). The move looks like continuation of a powerful thematic/momentum re-rating rather than a discrete news event.

Copart rose ~7% with no fresh company announcement; commentary attributed the jump to an oversold bounce plus institutional buying as investors re-digested the quarter's EPS beat ($0.43 vs $0.41) and resilient margins after a sharp prior selloff. Essentially a rebound/relief rally in a beaten-down name.

Cognex gained ~6.6% on continued post-Q2 follow-through: the quarter showed record margins and strong free cash flow (FCF up ~70% y/y) despite a slight revenue miss, and analysts moved price targets higher (e.g., DA Davidson to $65) amid AI machine-vision/automation enthusiasm. No new same-day company release was found.

AMD jumped ~6.5% as the market digested its $4.75 billion four-tranche note offering (weighted-average coupon ~5.04%, settling Aug 17), with proceeds seen funding the MI450 accelerator ramp; investors read the cheap, well-absorbed financing as a green light for the AI datacenter product cycle.

Peabody rose with a broad energy-complex bid (crude higher, thermal coal futures around one-month highs near $130/t) alongside other upstream/oilfield names that also jumped that session; no Peabody-specific positive announcement was found (the only company news was a reminder of a securities class-action lead-plaintiff deadline).

Solaris Energy Infrastructure extended gains on the data-center power theme following its record Q2, raised guidance, expanded power-contract scope, an equity investment in Deployable Energy, and a string of bullish analyst reaffirmations/PT raises (Barclays to $90, Stifel Buy). No discrete same-day catalyst identified.

MP Materials rallied as part of a sector-wide rare-earth surge that day (USA Rare Earth ~+9%, NioCorp ~+3%), driven by ongoing US critical-minerals policy/stockpile and China export-restriction narratives plus momentum from MP's recent revenue beat and aerospace magnet deal.
Fox Class A shares climbed after JPMorgan upgraded the stock and raised its price target, with shares up ~4% pre-market and finishing up ~5.5%.

NRG rose ~5.4% as investors revisited its data-center power pipeline (including a 1.2 GW Texas hyperscaler project and 'Bring Your Own Power' strategy) and its reaffirmed 2026 guidance, after a sharp drawdown from February highs; a rebound within the AI-power theme rather than a same-day news event.

Vishay rose ~5.3% with no company-specific news found for the day; the move tracked strength in pockets of the semiconductor trade (analog/discrete and equipment names) and lingering enthusiasm after its Q2 beat (adjusted EPS $0.19) and a recent Buy initiation with a $45 target.

Reports (WSJ, then Reuters) on Aug 18, 2026 said private equity firm KKR made a takeover offer for UGI Corp at roughly $42.50 per share, valuing the utility/propane distributor at about $9 billion; the stock spiked and even triggered a volatility halt.

No clear ticker-specific catalyst found for Aug 18; the move looks like continued follow-through from the Aug 6-7 Q2 report (better profitability, narrower loss, reaffirmed ~$1.08B guidance) amid strength in diabetes-technology names that day. Only routine filings (a tiny Rule 144 notice) were dated Aug 18.

Citigroup's quant team upgraded Bath & Body Works to Buy from Neutral with a ~$25 target ahead of the Aug 27 Q2 report, arguing the post-earnings selloff was overdone and citing improving Placer store-traffic data.

Morgan Stanley raised its Planet Fitness price target to $51 from $47 (keeping Equal Weight), which investors treated as incremental support after the Aug 6 Q2 beat (EPS $0.88 vs $0.85, revenue $365.2M vs $356.2M).

No clear catalyst found for Aug 18; Shift4 had been hammered to just above its 52-week low near $45 after a weak Q2/guidance cut, and the day's gain appears to be an oversold bounce plus general fintech/payments sentiment rather than fresh company news.

No specific news catalyst found; RB Global rose from near its 52-week low ($82.03) to about $85.76, with coverage attributing the move to valuation/'strong fundamentals' after Q2 (11% GTV growth, raised 2026 guidance) and an upcoming Aug 25 dividend ex-date.

Intuit rose ~4.4% after announcing a broad expansion of its AI 'Intuit Intelligence' capabilities across mid-market products — Intuit Enterprise Suite and QuickBooks Online Advanced, including Intuit Intelligence Chat — a week ahead of its Aug 25 fiscal Q4 report.

No clear catalyst found; news screeners explicitly flagged 'no clear catalyst identified' for Chewy's Aug 18 gain. The move looks like a continued rebound off June's multiyear low ahead of the Aug 27 Q2 report.

No fresh Aug 18 news; commentary attributed the gain to continued investor follow-through from Monster's early-August Q2 beat (adj. EPS $0.60 vs $0.58, record $2.54B revenue), the 2-for-1 split, and subsequent price-target hikes.

No single dated catalyst found; coverage around Aug 17-18 pointed to a string of analyst price-target increases (consensus lifted to about $41.54, one target at $45) plus buybacks/dividend support after the Q2 beat, with the stock pushing back toward its 52-week high.

Moderna and Merck announced that the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial of their individualized mRNA cancer vaccine intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157/V940) plus Keytruda hit its primary endpoint in resected melanoma — the first late-stage success for an mRNA cancer vaccine. The landmark interim readout nearly tripled sentiment on Moderna's pipeline and the stock roughly doubled.

Estée Lauder reported fiscal Q4 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.39 vs. ~$0.32 expected on revenue of about $3.63B, beating estimates, and raised its fiscal 2027 operating-margin outlook on the back of its restructuring/profit-recovery plan.

Hecla closed up 14.43% at $20.54 on ~1.9x average volume as spot silver jumped roughly 4-6% to the mid-$60s after the U.S. Treasury said it would double buybacks of long-dated debt, sending 10- and 30-year yields and the dollar lower; Hecla's zero-net-debt balance sheet was cited as added leverage to the metal.

Hims & Hers jumped ~13-14% after CEO Andrew Dudum's CNBC appearance in which he forcefully pushed back on the FTC lawsuit against the company, with commentary also noting the company benefits from continued FDA restrictions keeping compounded GLP-1 competitors off the market.

Coeur Mining rose ~13% alongside Hecla in a broad precious-metals rally: gold settled up about 4% near $4,512/oz and silver up over 6% near $67/oz after the Treasury's expanded long-dated debt buyback announcement pushed real yields and the dollar down.

Merck gained on the same catalyst as Moderna — the positive Phase 3 readout for the Merck-partnered individualized mRNA cancer vaccine used in combination with its blockbuster Keytruda, which opens a potential adjuvant melanoma franchise and extends the Keytruda life cycle.

No clear company-specific catalyst found for the 8/19/26 move; WRBY traded from ~$25.65 to ~$28.69 intraday with commentary that day focused on post-Q2 valuation debate and continued excitement about the Google/Samsung AI smart-glasses launch, but no dated announcement, upgrade or filing was identified.

Alexandria, a heavily shorted, rate-sensitive life-science REIT, surged as long-end Treasury yields fell sharply (30-year down ~10bp to 5.18%) on the Treasury's doubled long-dated buyback program, compounded by a broad life-science/biotech sentiment lift from the Moderna-Merck cancer-vaccine data that benefits its biotech tenant base.
